title: Railhead weekly readiness docket (personal prep)
content:
Quick pocket notes for the Railhead readiness sync (my 1:1 prep + follow-ups). Not polished — meant for the meeting and immediate action capture.

Context and goal:
- Scope: final validation for the release train (Railhead) next week. Primary risks: serving runtime memory regression, autoscaler flakiness, and rollout policy mismatch for dedicated customers.
- Goal for this sync: clear go/no-go gates per component, confirm owners for action items, set an explicit rollback trigger and owner.

Agenda (30m total, tight):
1) 0-5m: Quick status round — call out any new blockers (each owner 30s)
2) 5-12m: Go/No-Go checklist review (service-by-service)
3) 12-22m: Action items & short-term mitigations (who does what by EOD)
4) 22-28m: Rollback & postmortem owner assignment
5) 28-30m: Sync up on communication plan (customer notices + internal channel)

Current snapshot (my notes):
- Serving runtime (owner: Jia): baseline latency + p50 stable in canary, but p99 increased ~120ms on longer sequences. Jira RK-4021 flagged. Need to confirm kernel selection fallback works under 95th percentile.
- Autoscaler (owner: Omar): observed 2x scale delay in 2/3 reproduction runs. Trigger thresholds may be too conservative for microburst loads. PR #889 contains the threshold tweak but needs perf test.
- Rollout config (owner: me): default rollout uses region-first then model-variant fallback after 3m. Confirmed with QA on staging; still need a test for cross-region fallback.
- Dedicated customer config: ensure reserved capacity pin is honored — 2 customers on dedicated will require manual throttle if autoscaler misfires.

Go / No-Go checklist (quick yes/no + callouts):
- Critical test pass: runtime memory regression tests (yes/partial/no) -> partial (p99 latency regression) -> mitigation: enable kernel fallback and re-run subset. Owner: Jia, ETA: 2026-03-12 18:00 PT
- Autoscaler responsiveness (yes/partial/no) -> partial -> mitigation: deploy PR #889 to staging and run microburst suite. Owner: Omar, ETA: 2026-03-12 20:00 PT
- Rollback plan exists and tested (yes/no) -> yes (manual rollback tested once, automation partial) -> action: final runbook update + smoke test. Owner: Evelyn, ETA: 2026-03-12 16:00 PT
- Customer comms templates reviewed (yes/no) -> no -> action: draft notice for dedicated customers and a short status blurb for status.redwood.ai. Owner: Jia -> draft by 17:00 PT

Quick risk matrix (for talking points):
- High risk: autoscaler causing capacity shortages during first 48h -> mitigation: enable conservative burst reserve and manual override schedule
- Medium risk: p99 latency regression impacting QA samples -> mitigation: kernel fallback + temporary model-length cap for specific routes
- Low risk: rollout config mismatch -> mitigation: smoke test cross-region fallback and holdback on 2 customers

Action items (capture during sync):
- Jia: enable kernel fallback flag on canary, run 3 long-seq tests, post results to #release-railhead (ETA 2026-03-12 18:00)
- Omar: deploy autoscaler threshold PR to staging and run microburst suite (ETA 2026-03-12 20:00)
- Evelyn (me): update rollback runbook with exact commands + checklist; add decision tree for partial vs full rollback (ETA 2026-03-12 16:00)
- Product (ask: Lin): confirm if we can delay rollout for dedicated customers by 24h if autoscaler instability persists (ACTION: Lin to respond in thread)
- SRE: schedule on-call shadow for first 72h of rollout and make rotation explicit in the runbook (Owner: Priya, ETA 2026-03-13 09:00)

Follow-up notes for 1:1s (with owners) — quick bullets I want to cover today:
- With Jia: confirm the exact test vectors for long-seq p99 tests; make sure we log kernel-choice metadata in traces
- With Omar: get the microburst run logs in a table format so I can share with product; determine if threshold tweak is safe for dedicated fleets
- With Lin (product): alignment on customer holdback policy and who signs off on delaying rollout

Communication playbook (very short):
- If go: post short status on status.redwood.ai + internal #release-railhead once rollout starts. Dedicated customers get proactive email with dates and support contact.
- If partial hold: send immediate note to dedicated customers saying we postponed for reliability checks + offer optional early access window when stable.
- If no-go: brief execs + customer success and propose new window; owner: Evelyn for exec note, Customer Success for customer outreach

Open questions / stuff to think about (notes-to-self):
- Do we have a metric threshold for rollback that is not just p99 but also error-rate and waste (cost) spike? (add to runbook)
- If kernel fallback fixes p99 but doubles CPU, is that acceptable short-term? Need product signoff on cost impact.
- Should we pre-warm dedicated pools for the first 6h of rollout to avoid cold-start spikes? Trade-off vs cost.

Meeting prep to do before sync (very short checklist):
- Pull last 6h traces for the affected routes (Jia)
- Prepare a one-slide summary of the risk matrix (me)
- Confirm SRE on-call for rollout window (Priya)
- Draft customer email skeleton (Jia -> make terse)

Notes after the run (placeholder to capture during meeting):
- DECISION: (GO / PARTIAL / NO-GO) -> __________
- Immediate next step owner(s): __________
- Follow-up check-in window: (time) -> __________

Random scratch lines (brain dump):
- If we hold launch, propose narrowed beta to 5% traffic to exercise autoscaler only, not full rollout.
- Keep rollback automation as opt-in for first 24h.
- Remember to update the rollout dashboard with the exact git SHA and config flags.

---
If this doc is useful, convert to a formal runbook page after decisions final. For now: quick, messy, actionable.

E.
